questions.help:
7 Seat belts
 
7.4 The correct fastening of seat belts
The seat belt must be properly secured (buckled-up) and adjusted correctly so that it is neither too loose nor too tight for comfortable travel.
If the seat belt is slack the body travels a greater distance during an impact and is more likely to be hit against the steering wheel or windshield.
If seatbelts are not snugly fastened, the seatbelt loses effectiveness and can lead to injuries in accidents.
The use of seat belt locking clips or tension adjusters is prohibited and dangerous, because it reduces the effectiveness of the seat belt.
(Página 77 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Journeys and defensive and efficient driving    
     
DEFENSIVE DRIVING  
4 Observation  
4.3 Use of mirrors and monitor the blind spot
Convex glass is generally used in the exterior mirrors. This makes objects appear smaller and further away, but in reality there are closer than they look. The advantage is that they offer a greater field of vision. Sometimes they also have a double curvature that aids to minimise blind spots.
Interior mirrors are typically flat, and provide a view of what is happening behind without distorting sizes and distances, although the viewing angle is smaller.
Despite the adjustment of mirrors, there always remains, on each side of the vehicle, an area where objects can be lost to the driver. This is called a ‘blind spot’ and the existence of this poses a danger, because the driver cannot see what is in this area.
(Página 272 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
La distancia de frenado es…
The braking distance is…
questions.help:
12 Distances
 
12.2 The braking distance
The braking distance is the distance the vehicle travels from the point at which the driver first applies the brakes, until the vehicle come to a complete stop.
This distance can vary depending on:
The speed of the vehicle at the point the brakes are applied.
The mass of the vehicle and its load.
The technical condition of the vehicle (brakes, tyres, shock absorbers, etc.)
The environmental conditions and the condition of the road surface (snow, rain, state of the surface, etc.)
The driver (psychophysical status –mental and physical state, experience, etc.)
An increase in speed causes the braking distance to increase, but this is at a greater rate than the speed increase.
Thus, when the velocity is doubled the braking distance is four times higher.
(Página 179 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
¿Qué medidas debe adoptar si se produce un accidente?

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions  
 
8 The rule - PAH
Correct behaviour in the first 10 minutes directly after a collision is of vital importance as it:
Saves lives.
Avoids further collisions.
Reduces (up to 30%) or completely prevents secondary casualties.
Reduces damage to property.
Anyone who arrives at the site of an accident should apply the rule, which is represented by the abbreviation P.A.H. – protect, advise and help.
(Página 258 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
El consumo de drogas de abuso, ¿tiene relación con los accidentes más graves?
Is the consumption of illegal drugs related to the most serious accidents?
questions.help:
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS    
 
17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
The consumption of illegal drugs is related to many of the most serious accidents. A person driving under the influence of drugs puts all those around him/her at serious risk of accidents.
One of the effects of drugs is that risk perception decreases and some drugs can cause the driver to have an incorrect perception of time and space. The consumption of drugs will never improve reaction time. For people who take drugs and drive, the probability of having an accident is greater. It is forbidden to drive any vehicle with presence of drugs in the body. Substances excluded are those used under medical prescription and for therapeutic purposes, provided that the driver is able to manage the vehicle and drive with diligence, precaution and without distractions.
Driving with drugs present in the body may result in the loss of 6 points.
(Página 43 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
Si circulando le sorprende el sueño debe:
If you are driving and you start to feel tired:
questions.help:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES
 
12 Remedies to counteract fatigue and drowsiness
The recommendations to prevent accidents due to fatigue or lack of sleep can be summarised by three simple rules:
At least every 2 hours or every 200 kilometres take a rest of at least 20 or 30 minutes. These intervals should be shortened if the driver shows any signs or symptoms of fatigue and sleepiness.
If the signs for fatigue or sleepiness appear locate a convenient place to park and sleep for a period of time (20 or 30 minutes are usually sufficient). Continuing without resting multiplies the risk of a traffic collision occurring.
(Página 40 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
En vías con tráfico denso, ¿se puede hacer uso del claxon?
On roads with heavy traffic, are you allowed to use your horn?
questions.help:
21 Audible warning instrument - horn
 
The purpose of the audible warning instrument, horn, is to warn others of the presence of your vehicle.
The sound emitted must be uniform and of sufficient intensity. Only certain vehicles are permitted to emit a sound of varied pitch – such as emergency service vehicles.
Occasionally signs (R-310) may be displayed which forbids the sounding of the horn, except to prevent an accident.
(Página 106 del manual 'Learning to drive')

21 Audible warning instrument - horn
 
The horn can only be used in certain circumstances, as a warning to:
Avoid a possible accident; such as in narrow roads, hump back bridges or roads with bends with little or no visibility.
To warn, on roads outside of a built-up-area, that the vehicle behind is overtaking or planning to do so.
To warn other road users, that the vehicle is being used as a highpriority vehicle –normally reserved for emergency service vehicles.
(Página 106 del manual 'Learning to drive')
